And that way, when patients search for a practice locally through the AI, it’s someone that they’re able to find based on a certain competence, a certain adequacy, and a certain distinction.But does that clarify a little bit more about the significance of the call and what’s going on? scripts.title: I’m not interested (second or third time)
scripts.content:
Got it. So, let me clarify because I’m sensing the caliber of the call isn’t fully being understood: Right now, if you’ve noticed when you search on AI, the only medical offices that come up when a patient searches locally, are corporate run practices or subpar practices not privately held practices such as yours. Right? The problem is that those corporate run practices are usually a factory and leave patients with a sour taste in their mouth. But, ironically, these same patients actually never end up at private practice with a much better experience because the search engines and social media brands have essentially sold themselves off to whoever is willing to pay.

So now, because there have been so many complaints about this issue from both Doctors AND patients, the practice referral network was created so that only the top practices that actually do qualitative work, will be seen when patients are searching. Does that clarify a little bit more about the significance of the call?

scripts.title: Is this a paid thing? How much does this cost?
scripts.content: Ohhhh, so this isn’t a marketing or paid advertising thing, it’s just an interview so that we can refer patients to the right practices. Now to just confirm, you’re the sole owner of the practice right?

scripts.content: Maybe there's a little bit of confusion regarding what's going on. So, you're not doing us a favor by doing the interview. We’re doing you a favor by doing the interview. If you feel that you need to be reimbursed for this, I would put your best foot forward for the interview and ensure that you're doing your best to be selected because that'll be the best repayment that you can get. We understand your time is valuable. While the interview is free, it offers a great opportunity to learn more about your practice and you'll help us identify the best practices to refer patients to, including your own.

So, are mornings or afternoons better for you?

scripts.title: Are you from OpenAI/ChatGPT Yes or no??
scripts.content: As I mentioned I manage the entire healthcare research division for ChatGPT, and look, I know you guys get a lot of calls for a lot of different things and I know that can be frustrating for you, but it’s equally frustrating for me to be bundled up with those calls…. so that’s why I’m trying to clarify what’s going on since it’s a very big deal but, this is just an interview. So, are mornings or afternoons better for you?

scripts.title: You need to speak with my office manager
scripts.content: So I wish I could.. It would make my life a lot easier if we could just speak with the front desk or office manager as opposed to the Doctor, but because it’s a Doctor referral network, the interview obviously needs to be Doctor verified. Does that make sense?

scripts.title: How does it work? So, you’re going to interview me… what happens after?
scripts.content: So, we’re going to do the interview with you, review it with our team, compare it to the other 4 practices we are considering in the area, and if you are selected, we’ll let you know. And then, when patients search for a top Doctor in your area, you will be the one that appears. Does that make sense?

scripts.title: Why are you doing this? What are you selecting me for?
scripts.content: Yeah, so the reason we are actually setting up a call as opposed to blindly selecting practices, is because we want to make sure all of the providers that we include, are of a certain competence, caliber, and distinction. Does that make sense?

scripts.title: How did you select me? / How did you find me? / Why are you selecting me?
scripts.content: We have a team of research analysts who use a 5 point metric system to determine who we ultimately reach out to. Obviously, I don’t want to waste your time or my time so, before we ever reach out to a practice, we will do a tremendous amount of research on our end. Does that make sense?

scripts.title: What did you look at exactly? How is the 5 point metric system calculated?
scripts.content: Great question, so we actually look at a bunch of different things like speaking to different doctors in the area, going to different conferences, looking at patient review sites to compile what we believe to be the higher end practices in each area… However we don’t want to believe everything we read online, so we interview to validate that you are who we’ve learnt you to be. Does that make sense?

scripts.title: How did you get my cell phone number?
scripts.content: My assistant Alyssa Rose had this listed as your business contact.. So I’m looking at the calendar now. Does [Time and day] or [Time and day] work better?

scripts.title: I already have ChatGPT
scripts.content: Yeah, of course, everyone has access to ChatGPT. The point here though is not whether you have or use ChatGPT or AI, the point is that there are patients actively searching for the top practices in the area on AI Search platforms and we’re selecting 1 of 5 practices to determine who is ultimately going to be the practice that we select. So just confirm, you’re the sole owner of the practice right?

scripts.title: So let’s do this in 2 weeks or something like that
scripts.content: So because it’s an exclusive initiative, we’re wrapping up the entire area by the end of the week next week, so I’m looking at my calendar now, what time do you usually finish seeing patients?

scripts.title: Are you guys from OpenAI/ChatGPT or are you a third party marketing company?
scripts.content: So to be clear, the healthcare research division is actually a consortium (Kon-Sore-Shee-Um) of all the major AI search platforms. It was actually created to address this issue of patients complaining about getting subpar medical experiences from these corporate practices. As these complaints have reached high enough up in the rankings, this initiative was formed by all of the major AI platforms. You’re actually 1 of 5 practices that we are considering for it which is why I am trying to get something scheduled this week or next. So, for tomorrow, are you better in the morning or afternoon?

scripts.title: Who are the other practices that you’re selecting for this?
scripts.content: Great question. Once we decide who we select, we then will release it to the public. We don’t share who we are interviewing so that we don’t skew the results. Just to confirm, you’re the owner of the practice, right?

scripts.title: I will be driving during the interview / Can I do this while driving?
scripts.content: Because of liability in different states, unfortunately we cannot do the interview while you are driving. What time will you be stationed up back at home or at your office?

scripts.title: I work in emergency medicine and don't need referrals
scripts.content: So to be clear, this isn't about new referrals. This is about the fact that right now what we found from the data is that when people are searching for an emergency doctor, they need the information, and they need it very, very quickly and they make very rush decisions. And when they make those rush decisions, they sometimes fall into the hands of practices that are not relevant for them. So what we're doing is we're choosing one practice in each region to select who is the practice that we're gonna be selecting. So when someone immediately runs to their computer to figure out where they will be seeking emergency care local to them, it's not going to present an entire list. It's going to present one high value, high quality practice that can be relied upon. And that's why we're interviewing. We're keenly aware how emergency practices work. Now, does that clarify a little bit more of why I'm reaching out to you now? But does that clarify the benefit specifically for you guys?

scripts.title: I get a call back and have no idea who's calling me. Try to reference the lead sheet but it's borderline impossible while I'm trying to stay talking on the phone - Asking who's calling me is also not a good look
scripts.content: I get a lot of inbound calls from a lot of people wanting to do an interview with us, and unfortunately I have to screen these calls somehow. You know, like, take that approach where it’s more like, look, I get a lot of calls from a lot of junior practices wanting to do an interview with me, and I’m not sure exactly who this is, and I just been fooled by a lot of different practices that I didn’t personally call. And then, you know, I’m spending time with the practice that I have no interest in speaking to. So I’d appreciate it if you let me know who you are so I can know if you’re the right person that I called earlier today. What’s your name?

scripts.title: My practice is already listed in the top five
scripts.content: Right, Doctor, and that’s actually something we hear from time to time. Your ChatGPT experience can be personalized based on your account activity and previous conversations. So seeing your own practice in your results doesn’t necessarily mean a brand-new patient searching from a different account is seeing the same recommendation. What we’re interested in is how your practice is represented when someone who doesn’t already know you is looking for a provider in your area. The interview gives us an opportunity to learn more about the practice. It’s only about 45 minutes—would 3:00 or 4:00 be easier for you?

scripts.title: What is the benefit for me?
scripts.content: So the benefit is that right now, the whole model of people finding a practice that promotes itself, this pay-to-play model, is being completely eradicated. There is no option for that anymore because there have been too many people who have been ending up at subpar practices that are really just junior practices telling people that they’re the world just because they have a lot of money to do so. And what happens is that patients go there, they have a negative experience, and they blame us for that reason. So, we’re completely eliminating the model of you being able to pay. So now when someone is searching for someone locally, only the practices that we select are gonna be the ones that are discoverable. We’re interviewing five practices in each region, and you are one of five the practices that we’re considering for this. So to answer your question, the benefit is that when someone searches locally for a practice in whichever category they’re searching, the practice that we select is the one that’s gonna be discoverable. It’s a very, very big deal.

scripts.title: How are you making money? / How do you monetize? What’s the catch?
scripts.content:
Great question.. have you ever heard of the attention economy before?

No I haven't.

Ok.. the reason why AI platforms don't charge you to create an account is because they are incentivized by your usage. The more users that are using the platform, the more money they make from third party advertisers. For that reason, we are creating a doctor referral network nationwide that's based off of a highly vetted interview process, so that it creates more value for our users. Does that make sense?

Of course. A lot of doctors ask us the same thing, like, What's the catch? Have you heard of the attention economy before? Basically, it's similar to how platforms like Youtube, Instagram and Tiktok make money. A lot of it is based on traffic, engagement, and the amount of time people spend on the platform, along with ads.

For us, the more people use the platform and come to it to discover and connect with Doctors, the more value the platform generates. That's how the platform makes money.

But that's really just a small part of what the interview is about. The interview itself is simply an organic conversation where we learn more about you and your practice.

scripts.title: What’s the purpose of this call / why are you reaching out?
scripts.content: So, the purpose is to make a reliable network where patients can find practices based on merit as opposed to just the corporate practices who are paying the most to be found and end up giving patients a sour taste in their mouth. That’s the reason we’re doing this. Yeah, so the reason we are actually setting up a call as opposed to blindly selecting practices, is because we want to make sure all of the providers that we include, are of a certain competence, caliber, and distinction.
